questions.title: Reverse Word Characters Drill
questions.description:
Given a single non-empty word consisting only of lowercase English letters, print the word with its characters reversed.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
The reversed word on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 1000

questions.title: Palindrome Word Check Drill
questions.description:
Given a single non-empty word of lowercase English letters, determine whether it is a palindrome (reads the same forward and backward).

Input Format:
A single line containing one word (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
Print "Yes" if the word is a palindrome, otherwise print "No".

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 1000

questions.title: Anagram Pair Check Drill
questions.description:
Given two lowercase words of equal length, determine whether they are anagrams (contain the same multiset of letters).

Input Format:
Two lines, each containing one lowercase word.

Output Format:
Print "Yes" if they are anagrams, otherwise print "No".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each word <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Count Character Occurrences Drill
questions.description:
Given a string s and a character c, count how many times c occurs in s.

Input Format:
Line 1: the string s.
Line 2: a single character c.

Output Format:
A single integer — the number of occurrences.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

questions.title: Uppercase to Lowercase Conversion
questions.description:
Given a string containing letters, spaces and punctuation, convert every uppercase letter A-Z to its lowercase equivalent and leave all other characters unchanged.

Input Format:
A single line containing the input string.

Output Format:
The transformed string on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

questions.title: Replace Vowels with Asterisk
questions.description:
Given a string, replace every vowel (a, e, i, o, u in either case) with the character '*' and leave all other characters unchanged.

Input Format:
A single line containing the input string.

Output Format:
The transformed string on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

questions.title: Domain Name Reversal Inspector
questions.description:
A network engineer inspects a hostname by reading it character-by-character from right to left to verify the top-level suffix. Given a single hostname token (letters and dots only), print the hostname reversed.

Input Format:
A single line containing one hostname token (no spaces).

Output Format:
The reversed hostname on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= hostname length <= 1000

questions.title: Coupon Code Palindrome Validator
questions.description:
An e-commerce store issues promotional coupon codes that are guaranteed to be palindromes (so the code reads the same forwards and backwards). Given a coupon code (alphanumeric, no spaces), validate it.

Input Format:
A single line containing the coupon code.

Output Format:
Print "Valid" if it is a palindrome, otherwise "Invalid".

Constraints:
1 <= code length <= 1000

questions.title: Scrabble Tile Anagram Verifier
questions.description:
Two Scrabble players each lay down their tile racks. Determine whether their two racks contain exactly the same multiset of letters (only lowercase letters are compared).

Input Format:
Two lines, each containing one player's rack as a single string of lowercase letters.

Output Format:
Print "Match" if the racks are anagrams, otherwise "NoMatch".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each rack <= 1000
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each rack <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Chat Exclamation Mark Counter
questions.description:
A moderation tool flags chat messages containing many exclamation marks as potential shouting. Given a single-line chat message, count how many '!' characters appear.

Input Format:
A single line containing the chat message.

Output Format:
A single integer — the number of '!' characters.

Constraints:
1 <= message length <= 1000

questions.title: DNA Strand Reverse Complement
questions.description:
A bioinformatics tool computes the reverse complement of a DNA strand. Given a strand consisting only of the characters A, C, G, T (uppercase), reverse the strand and then complement each base: A<->T and C<->G. Print the result.

Input Format:
A single line containing the DNA strand.

Output Format:
The reverse complement strand on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= strand length <= 1000, characters in {A, C, G, T}

questions.title: Sentence Palindrome Moderator
questions.description:
A moderation tool flags reviews whose letter pattern is a palindrome when spaces, punctuation and letter case are ignored. Given a single-line sentence, decide whether it is a palindrome considering only letters (case-insensitive).

Input Format:
A single line containing the sentence.

Output Format:
Print "Yes" if it is a palindrome, otherwise "No".

Constraints:
1 <= sentence length <= 2000
questions.sampleinput1: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
questions.input1: Was it a car or a cat I saw

questions.title: Slogan Anagram Comparator
questions.description:
Two marketing slogans are considered equivalent if they contain the same multiset of letters (ignoring spaces and letter case). Given two single-line slogans, decide whether they are letter-anagrams.

Input Format:
Two lines, each containing one slogan.

Output Format:
Print "Yes" if they are letter-anagrams, otherwise "No".

Constraints:
1 <= length of each slogan <= 2000
questions.input1:
the morse code
here come dots

questions.title: Ciphertext Frequency Analyst
questions.description:
A cryptanalyst performs frequency analysis on a ciphertext. Given a string of lowercase letters only, find the most frequent letter. If there is a tie, output the alphabetically smallest letter.

Input Format:
A single line containing the ciphertext (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
The most frequent letter (a single character on its own line).

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

questions.title: ROT13 Message Encoder
questions.description:
A forum obfuscates spoilers by applying the ROT13 cipher: each letter is shifted by 13 positions in the alphabet, wrapping around. Non-letter characters are unchanged, and letter case is preserved. Given a message, output its ROT13 encoding.

Input Format:
A single line containing the message.

Output Format:
The ROT13-encoded message on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= |message| <= 1000

questions.title: Kebab to Snake Case Converter
questions.description:
A front-end tool converts CSS class names written in kebab-case (lowercase letters and hyphens) into snake_case identifiers (lowercase letters and underscores). Given a kebab-case string, replace every hyphen '-' with an underscore '_'.

Input Format:
A single line containing the kebab-case string.

Output Format:
The snake_case string on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

questions.title: Sentence Word Order Reverser
questions.description:
A language translator must reverse the order of words in a sentence while preserving each word's characters. Words are separated by single spaces. There is no leading or trailing whitespace. Given a sentence, print the words in reverse order separated by single spaces.

Input Format:
A single line containing the sentence (words separated by single spaces).

Output Format:
The sentence with words in reverse order.

Constraints:
1 <= sentence length <= 2000

questions.title: Anagram Group Counter
questions.description:
A linguist receives a list of n lowercase words (no spaces, length 1 to 100). Two words are anagrams if they share the same multiset of letters. Count the number of distinct anagram classes (each word belongs to exactly one class).

Input Format:
Line 1: an integer n.
Next n lines: one lowercase word per line.

Output Format:
A single integer — the number of distinct anagram classes.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= word length <= 100
questions.input2:
6
abc
bca
cab
abd
dba
bad

questions.title: Run Length Encoding Compressor
questions.description:
Compress a string of lowercase letters using run-length encoding: each maximal run of the same character is replaced by the character followed by the run length (when the run length is greater than 1). Single occurrences of a character are emitted as just the character (no count).

Input Format:
A single line containing the input string (lowercase letters only).

Output Format:
The RLE-compressed string on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 1000

questions.title: Title Case Normalizer for CMS
questions.description:
A blog CMS converts user-entered titles to Title Case, normalizing any run of whitespace (spaces or tabs) into a single space, trimming leading and trailing whitespace. The first letter of each word is uppercased, the remaining letters are lowercased, and non-letter characters are preserved.

Input Format:
A single line containing the raw title (may contain leading/trailing/internal whitespace and mixed case).

Output Format:
The normalized Title Case title on a single line.

Constraints:
1 <= |title| <= 2000
